title: Partial reconstruction: surface recoverable file states even when full reconstruction fails
description:
Add "reconstruct up to..." functionality even if the full reconstruction fails. The reconstruction engine should be able to provide at least SOME reconstructed file states from the JSONL files it finds, even if the entire session cannot be reconstructed. The engine and webapp need a way to reflect this reconstruction state so the user knows what file states were recoverable and what were not.

Scope (refined with user):
- Failure modes to survive (all three): (1) parser-level crashes — unknown record types/keys in newer-CC JSONLs must not abort the load; skip the bad record, keep parsing, reconstruct from what loaded (today an unknown record type crashes the viewer before the consent dialog); (2) engine-stage failures — a reconstruction stage throwing mid-session keeps all file states computed up to that point; (3) missing-evidence gaps — sidecar backups / git repo / recorded tmpdir gone: reconstruct the revisions that don't need the missing evidence, mark the rest unrecoverable.
- Granularity: per-revision. Each revision of each file is marked recovered or unrecoverable, with a reason (matches the per-step coverage-ledger mindset).
- Webapp UI (chosen A+C from mockups in plans/partial-reconstruction-ui-mockups.html): session-level partial-reconstruction banner with counts; inline dashed gap rows in the timeline; dashed/grayed missing rev-cards in the revision stepper; plus a per-file coverage strip in the file list (one segment per revision, red = unrecoverable, click a red segment for a reason popover). Same engine output feeds both treatments.

title: Publish chain: push scenarios → JFRED → jfredToolsPlugin, verify clean-room + marketplace, sync wrapper clone
description:
Consolidated go-public checklist from four implementation-notes files:
(1) User must push the scenarios repo (1 unpushed commit 075ef56 "added S86, updated S41") BEFORE JFRED is pushed — JFRED's pin was fetched from the local clone and dangles for cloners until then.
(2) JFRED is staged but uncommitted; first commit + push still needs the privacy gate re-run at push time. Commit ordering: commit inside jfred/jfredToolsPlugin first, push, then re-stage the gitlink in JFRED (it currently records the license-only commit 70ad1b6), commit JFRED, then RevEng.
(3) Consider switching the GitHub default branch for matkatmusic/jfred from master (empty initial commit — a plain git clone gets an empty tool) to develop: `gh repo edit matkatmusic/jfred --default-branch develop`.
(4) After pushing jfredToolsPlugin to https://github.com/matkatmusic/jfredToolsPlugin, verify the install flow with a real `claude plugin marketplace add matkatmusic/jfredToolsPlugin` + `claude plugin install`, then decide whether the zshrc --plugin-dir wrapper (task 108's interim enablement) should be retired.
(5) ~/Programming/jfredToolsPlugin (the clone the claude() wrapper actually loads) does NOT yet have the two new scenario skills — pull/push the canonical $REVENG/jfred/jfredToolsPlugin changes into it after committing, or /impl-scenario and /plan-scenario won't resolve at the next launch (their RevEng copies are now archived).
(6) Deferred verifications left for the user from task 111: RevEng `npm test` (5 task-workflow tests + 2 python tests remain), `npm run typecheck`, clean-room `npm test`, and the interactive /run-scenario check under `command claude`.
